An invite marked for a profile-only member (target_member_id, ahaqqu/RumaQ#397) attaches the redeemer’s account to that existing member row — id, display name, birth date, and documents stay attached — instead of creating a new member.

get.description: Lists the members of a household — both linked accounts (has_account=true) and profile-only members without an account (has_account=false, ahaqqu/RumaQ#388). Members and owners of that household only.

post.description: Creates a profile-only member — a person with no user account (e.g. a toddler), identified by display_name plus an optional birth_date. Owner-only; the role is always member and such members never authenticate. They count toward member_count.

403.description: Only household owners can do that

patch.description: Updates a member’s profile fields (display_name, birth_date), addressed by member id. Owners may edit anyone; a linked member may edit themselves. Profile-only members (has_account=false) are owner-only. Roles are not writable.

403.description: Only household owners can edit other members

delete.description: Removes a member from a household, addressed by member id. Owner-only; the household must keep at least one owner (409 otherwise). Profile-only members are a simple delete; removing a linked member also repoints (or respawns) their session.

403.description: Only household owners can do that

409.description: A household must keep at least one owner

post.description: Leaves a household. The last owner cannot leave (409) until ownership is transferred. If the leaver has no households left, a fresh baseline one is created.

409.description: A household must keep at least one owner

get.description: Returns the household’s current live invite code, or null when none is active. Owner-only.

403.description: Only household owners can do that

post.description: Generates a fresh invite code for the household, revoking any previous live code. Owner-only. Codes expire after 7 days. An optional target_member_id marks the invite for one profile-only member of the household (ahaqqu/RumaQ#397): redeeming it attaches the redeemer’s account to that member row instead of creating a new member.

target_member_id.description: A profile-only member (has_account=false) of this household to mark the invite for; omit or null for a plain invite

403.description: Only household owners can do that

get.description: Lists the active household’s documents, newest first, each with its files in upload order. Optional filters: q (case-insensitive contains-search on the free-text document name — the #422 replacement for the category filter), memberId (both member modes — linked accounts and profile-only members), expiring_within (#426: N days, 1-365 — documents whose expiry lands within the next N days, already-expired included; orders those results soonest-expiry-first). Every item carries expires_on, remind_days_before and the COMPUTED days_until_expiry (whole days from the household calendar, pinned at UTC+7/WIB — the Indonesia-first audience; negative = expired) — never stored.

schema.description: Days ahead: documents expiring within N days (expired included)

post.description: Creates a document (multipart/form-data: name, file, optional label for that file, optional memberId). The name is free text — trimmed, 1-120 chars, no preset list (#422). The file becomes attachment #1 (sort_order 1); more files ride POST /documents/{id}/files, max 20 per document. Cap 10 MB enforced on Content-Length before the body is read and again on the parsed bytes; magic bytes must match the declared type (JPEG, PNG, WebP, PDF). memberId accepts both member modes (linked and profile-only). No public URLs exist — bytes are served only via the per-file content endpoint.

get.description: Returns one document’s metadata with its files in upload order. A document from another household answers the same 404 as a missing one (no existence leak).

patch.description: Updates a document’s expiry metadata (#426): expires_on (ISO YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear — clearing the expiry also clears the reminder window) and/or remind_days_before (integer days, 1-365). At least one field is required. Setting an expiry without a window applies the existing window, or the 30-day default when none was set; a window on a document without an expiry is a 400 (nothing to remind about). Expiry is metadata on the free-text document — the #422 naming and multi-file model are untouched. Every change writes an ‘update’ audit record in the same batch. Household-scoped like every vault route (a foreign household’s id answers 404, no existence leak); any household member may edit, matching the add-files authorization — the metadata is household-level information.

expires_on.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD expiry date; null clears it (and the window)

remind_days_before.description: Days before expiry the document enters the due-soon window

200.description: OK — the updated document comes back

delete.description: Hard-deletes a document: every file’s stored object AND the metadata rows, with the deletion audit record in the same batch (the file rows cascade). Uploader or household owner only. Audit rows outlive the document (the deletion record survives).

403.description: Only the uploader or a household owner can do that

post.description: Adds one file to an existing document (multipart/form-data: file, optional label). Max 20 files per document — a full document refuses another file with 409 before the body is read. Same 10 MB cap (Content-Length pre-check + parsed bytes) and magic-byte policy as create; the file lands at sort_order = max + 1 (upload order). Returns the updated document with all files. No public URLs exist — bytes are served only via the per-file content endpoint.

201.description: File added — the updated document comes back

409.description: The document already holds the maximum of 20 files

get.description: Streams one file’s bytes, authenticated and household-scoped (the file must belong to the document, the document to the household). Content-Type is the stored mime; disposition=inline previews (audited as view), disposition=attachment downloads (audited as download). Cache-Control is private, no-store — bytes never leak through any cache, and no public or presigned URL exists.

delete.description: Removes ONE file from a document: the stored object AND its row, with the file_delete audit record in the same batch. Allowed for the household owner, the document’s uploader, or the file’s uploader. The last file may be deleted — the document survives with zero files until someone deletes it. Audit rows outlive the file they name.

403.description: Only the household owner, the document uploader, or the file uploader can do that

get.description: Lists the active household’s tasks — the shared board (open + done). Filters compose: assignee=me (the caller’s member row), assignee=all (or absent — everyone), or a surrogate member id (both modes; an unknown id filters to an empty list, it is a read filter not a probe); status is open, done, or all (default all); mine=1 is the "My tasks" sugar for assignee=me and wins over assignee. No per-member read hiding: every household member sees the board (#429 design note).

schema.description: 'me', 'all', or a surrogate member id (both modes)

post.description: Creates a task: free-text title (trimmed, 1-120 chars — no preset categories, the #422 philosophy), optional assignee (ANY household member — linked or profile-only, 0021), optional due date and recurrence. Any linked member can create; profile-only members never act (no account, 0021). needs_approval derives server-side: true when the assignee is a profile-only member. The create audit record commits in the same batch.

assignee_member_id.description: A member of this household (both modes); omit or null for unassigned

patch.description: One endpoint, three actions. (1) Edit fields — title, due_date, recurrence, assignee_member_id (assign/reassign, null unassigns): creator or household owner; reassignment re-derives needs_approval from the new assignee’s mode and clears any prior approval; an empty patch is a no-op read. (2) Complete — status:"done" alone: the assignee (when linked), the creator, or an owner; profile-only assignees are completed on their behalf; a one-shot task flips to done, a RECURRING task rolls its due date to the next occurrence and stays open. (3) Approve — approve:true alone: creator or owner, only while needs_approval and the task is done; sets approved_by_member_id. Every action writes its audit row in the same batch.

assignee_member_id.description: A member of this household (both modes); null unassigns

200.description: OK — the updated task comes back

403.description: Only the creator/assignee/owner relationship allows that

409.description: The task’s state refuses the action (already done, not awaiting approval)

delete.description: Hard-deletes a task: creator or household owner. The deletion audit record commits in the SAME batch as the delete and survives it (household_task_audit.task_id is a plain TEXT handle — no FK), so the household’s completion history outlives the row.

403.description: Only the creator or a household owner can do that
